notes.11: Candidates correctly allowed for the invoice that had not been entered in the accounting records, but did not allow for the debit balances on the payables control account to be included with the receivables. Generally it is not permitted to “nett” accounts; candidates should include the gross figures to give the maximum information.
notes.14: The factory profit needed to take into account the mark-up on the opening and closing stocks of finished goods: $8000 + $48 000 - $9000 = $47 000.
notes.16: This question asked for Y’s share of the total profits but many candidates did not read the item carefully and thought that it was asking for his share of the residual net profit. Total profits include Y’s salary and his 6% interest on capital.
notes.general_comments:
The mean mark was 17, with many candidates bunching in the middle range. Only a few candidates
attained high or low marks.
There were no relatively easy questions on the paper. Candidates were required to have some basic
knowledge of accounting in order to answer any of the questions. The following questions prompted many
correct responses: 1, 5, 8, 13, 17, 20 and 22.
It is interesting to note that the management accounting questions do not have as high a correct response
rate as the financial accounting questions.
Some questions attracted incorrect responses from candidates, who were easily misled by an attractive
“distractor”. These were Questions 4, 15, 27, 28 and 29.
